;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**[[2018 Douma chemical attack]]
***The death toll from yesterday's suspected [[chemical weapon]]s attack in [[Douma, Syria]], rises to at least 70, according to the [[White Helmets (Syrian Civil War)|White Helmets]] group. The [[Syria]]n government and [[Russia]] deny the allegations of a chemical attack. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-43686157 (BBC)]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] warns [[Russia]] and [[Iran]] for backing [[President of Syria|Syrian president]] [[Bashar al-Assad]] and calls him "Animal Assad". [https://news.sky.com/story/trump-russia-will-pay-big-price-for-backing-animal-assad-11322689 (Sky News)]
**Eight missiles are launched at the [[Syria]]n [[Tiyas Military Airbase|T4 air base]] in [[Homs Governorate]], reportedly by [[Israeli Air Force|Israeli]] [[F-15]]s. Syria claimed that five of the missiles are intercepted by the [[Syrian Air Defense Force]]. Reports stated that 14 soldiers were killed in the strike, including 4 Iranian Revolution Guards. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-43694588 (BBC)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-syria/syria-russia-say-israeli-war-planes-carried-out-strike-on-syrian-air-base-idUSKBN1HG0D8 (Reuters)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/russia-syria-blame-israel-for-deadly-strike-on-syrian-air-base/ (''Times of Israel'')]
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**[[Israeli Defence Forces]] fire shells at [[Palestinians]] on foot near the border fence, saying the men had crossed the fence before reentering the [[Gaza Strip]] near [[Gaza City]]. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/palestinians-report-exchange-of-fire-with-idf-soldiers-near-gaza-borde-1.5978978 (''Haaretz'')]
**Gazan hospitals declare a state of emergency owing to the thousands injured. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/04/weve-stock-gaza-hospitals-declare-state-emergency-180408084314352.html (Al Jazeera)]
**The [[International Criminal Court]]'s chief prosecutor, [[Fatou Bensouda]], says conduct by both Israel and [[Hamas]] may amount to [[war crimes]] and warns anybody violating international law may face prosecution. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/at-gaza-border-idf-and-hamas-may-both-be-violating-international-law-icc-says/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**Israeli Defence Forces deny reports three [[Palestinian people|Palestinian]]s fired upon in Gaza yesterday by an Israeli tank had opened fire on Israeli soldiers and hardware, but says they planted two bombs made from plastic drinks bottles and containing an explosive liquid near the border fence. The suspects were not injured. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/idf-palestinians-who-breached-fence-planted-explosives/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**Israeli Defence Minister [[Avigdor Liberman]] asks Attorney General [[Avichai Mandelblit]] to probe NGO [[B’Tselem]] for "incitement to disobedience" for asking Israeli troops at the border to refuse orders. B’Tselem accuses Liberman in response of "a deep contempt for basic moral principles" and reiterates its call for IDF personnel to refuse to carry out "manifestly illegal orders". [https://www.timesofisrael.com/defense-minister-seeks-probe-into-btselem-for-urging-soldiers-to-refuse-orders/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[Palestinian Authority]] President [[Mahmoud Abbas]] says the PA will take no further responsibility for the [[Gaza Strip]] unless [[Hamas]] hands over full control. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/pa-wont-be-responsible-for-gaza-if-hamas-stays-in-charge-abbas-warns/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**Gazan journalists hold a protest against the shooting death of [[Yasser Murtaja]] at the border, which they face with their mouths taped shut. [http://www.jpost.com/Arab-Israeli-Conflict/Terrorist-or-journalist-Who-really-was-the-slain-Gazan-Yaser-Murtaja-549709 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Sinai insurgency]]
**The [[Egypt]]ian Army kills four suspected terrorists in the [[Sinai Peninsula]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-04/08/c_137096154.htm (Xinhua)]
*[[Terrorism in Germany]]
**[[Germany|German]] authorities arrest six men aged 18 to 21 suspected of planning a terror attack on today's [[Berlin Half Marathon]]. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2018/04/08/german-police-arrest-man-suspected-terror-plot-berlin-half-marathon/ (''The Telegraph'')]
*[[Terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**[[West Yorkshire Police|Police]] release two men detained for terrorism in [[Dewsbury]], saying they are confident no [[terrorism Acts|terrorism offences]] can be charged. [http://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2018-04-08/two-men-arrested-on-suspicion-of-terror-offences-released-without-charge/ (ITV)]
**A report commissioned by the [[United Kingdom|UK]] states terrorists and extremists are increasingly turning to [[Bitcoin]], the [[Darknet|dark net]], and [[encryption|encrypted communications apps]] in a bid to evade detection. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2018/apr/08/terrorists-plot-shadows-dark-net-report (''The Guardian'')]
**[[metropolitan Police|Police]] release on bail a suspected terrorist arrested yesterday at [[Gatwick Airport]] after he arrived on a flight from [[Morocco]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-43692584 (BBC)]
*[[Timeline of the Israeli–Palestinian conflict|Terrorism in Israel]]
**A [[Palestinian people|Palestinian]] man launches a stabbing attack in the West Bank settlement of [[Ma'aleh Adumim]] and is shot by a civilian. The attacker is hospitalised, as are three Israelis who suffered [[Acute stress reaction|shock]]. [http://www.israelnationalnews.com/News/News.aspx/244104 (Israel National News)]
**Authorities charge Ahmed Kunba with several attacks including a drive-by shooting in the West Bank settlement of [[Havat Gilad]] that killed one, shooting at a bus, and trying to infiltrate the West Bank settlement of [[Mevo Dotan|Dotan]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/associate-in-havat-gilad-terror-attack-charged-as-accomplice-to-murder/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[Iraqi insurgency (2017–present)]]
**[[Iraq]]i security forces kill six suspected terrorists and seize guns and explosives in an operation targeting [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]] in [[Anbar (town)|Anbar]]. [https://www.iraqinews.com/iraq-war/iraqi-troops-kill-seven-islamic-state-militants-in-anbar/ (Iraqi News)]
**A suicide bomber injures six [[Iraq]]i soldiers near [[Ramadi]], [[Al Anbar Governorate|Anbar]]. The soldiers were combing a building hit by a separate bombing yesterday that killed five and injured seven including a politician. [https://www.iraqinews.com/iraq-war/six-iraqi-soldiers-injured-as-suicide-bomber-blows-himself-up-in-anbar/ (Iraqi News)]
**Iraqi authorities say an unexplained explosion in Mutaibija, on the border of [[Diyala Governorate|Diyala]] and [[Saladin Governorate|Salahuddin]], killed an alleged senior member of [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|the Islamic State]]. [https://www.iraqinews.com/iraq-war/prominent-islamic-state-leader-killed-in-explosion-on-salahuddin-borders-official/ (Iraqi News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A bus collides with a train near [[Armyansk]], [[Crimea]], killing five people and injuring four others. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-04/08/c_137095917.htm (Xinhua)]
*[[2018 Paris–Roubaix]]
**[[Belgium|Belgian]] [[Vérandas Willems–Crelan]] cyclist [[Michael Goolaerts]] crashes during the race in [[France]] and subsequently dies in hospital. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cycling/43691211 (BBC)]
*[[2018 Bahrain Grand Prix]]
**[[Scuderia Ferrari|Ferrari]] [[Formula One]] driver [[Kimi Räikkönen]] hits a mechanic during a [[pit stop]]. The mechanic receives multiple leg fractures. [http://www.espn.co.uk/f1/story/_/id/23078875/ferrari-mechanic-suffers-broken-leg-pit-lane-collision (ESPN)]
*The [[United Kingdom|UK]] [[Airprox]] Board reveals a [[Red Arrows]] jet came within 100ft of [[midair collision|collision]] with a civilian plane last year. [https://www.lincolnshirelive.co.uk/news/local-news/red-arrow-jet-misses-civilian-1432591 (Lincolnshire Live)]

;International relations
*[[Sino-Indian border dispute]]
**The [[India]]n Army rejects [[China|Chinese]] categorisations of its patrols in [[Sino-Indian_border_dispute#Asaphila_in_Upper_Subansiri|Asaphila]] near the disputed [[Arunachal Pradesh]] border as "transgressions", and accuses China of damaging Indian roadlaying equipment. [http://indianexpress.com/article/india/china-objects-to-indias-transgression-in-arunachal-pradesh-india-rejects-protest-5128733/ (''The India Express'')]
*[[Russia-United Kingdom relations]]
**[[Russia]] accuses the [[United Kingdom]] of withholding information on the investigation into the murder of Russian exile [[Nikolay Glushkov]], which is being probed by counterterrorism officers. Glushkov had political asylum and was wanted in Russia for [[embezzlement]] from [[Aeroflot]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/russia-scotland-yard-nikolai-glushkov-latest-mysterious-death-aeroflot-fraud-vladimir-putin-a8294526.html (''The Independent'')]

;Law and crime
*[[2018 Münster attack]]
**[[Germany|German]] Interior Minister [[Horst Seehofer]] rejects claims that yesterday's car attack was an act of either [[Islamic extremism|Islamic]] or [[white supremacy|far-right]] terrorism, saying the attacker was not politically motivated. [http://www.thejournal.ie/muenster-investigation-3946639-Apr2018/ (''The Journal'')]
*[[Operation Car Wash]]
**Former [[President of Brazil]] [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]] surrenders to police following a two-day stand-off at a steelworkers' union building in [[São Bernardo do Campo]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-43686174 (BBC)]
*[[Animal welfare and rights in Australia]]
**A ship due to carry 65,000 sheep to the [[Middle East]] fails an [[Australian Maritime Safety Authority]] inspection after docking in [[Fremantle]], [[Western Australia]] and is denied permits for the voyage. The government is investigating newly emerged footage of conditions on the ship, where thousands of sheep died during a similar voyage last year. [http://www.abc.net.au/news/2018-04-08/maritime-officials-block-live-export-65000-sheep-to-middle-east/9631602 (ABC)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Hungarian parliamentary election, 2018]]  
**Voters in [[Hungary]] go to the polls for a [[National Assembly (Hungary)|parliamentary]] election with the [[Fidesz]] Party led by [[Viktor Orbán]] achieving a super-majority for the third election in a row. [http://www.focus-fen.net/news/2018/04/08/429209/afp-hungarians-to-vote-in-keenly-watched-poll.html (AFP via Focus News)], [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/the-latest-orban-says-election-is-about-hungarys-future/2018/04/08/84f76ec0-3af3-11e8-af3c-2123715f78df_story.html?utm_term=.4d97a6a4e044 (''Washington Post'')]
*[[First presidency of Donald Trump|Presidency of Donald Trump]]
**[[White House]] [[White House Press Secretary|press secretary]] [[Sarah Huckabee Sanders]] announces the departure of [[National Security Council]] spokesman [[Michael Anton]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/08/politics/michael-anton-departs-nsc/index.html (CNN)]

;Sport
*In [[golf]], American [[Patrick Reed]] wins the [[2018 Masters Tournament]] held in [[Augusta, Georgia]]. [https://www.sbnation.com/golf/2018/4/7/17209958/masters-2018-live-scores-leaderboard-sunday-highlights-news (SBNation)]
